subject: Agriculture
title: The Population Bomb Fear
description: A short lesson to help you apply The Population Bomb Fear.

hook.text: In 1968, Paul Ehrlich predicted hundreds of millions would starve in the 1970s. The world panicked.

buildup.text: World population was doubling every 35 years. Food production wasn't keeping pace—or so it seemed.

discovery.text: Ehrlich's dire predictions sparked global urgency. Governments poured money into agricultural research.

twist.text: The mass famine never came. A scientific revolution was already underway—one Ehrlich hadn't accounted for.

climax.text: The Green Revolution would prove that science could outrun population growth—at least for a while.

punchline.text: The prediction was wrong. The panic it caused was useful.

quiz.question: What did Paul Ehrlich predict in 'The Population Bomb'?
options: Mass starvation in the 1970s from population growth
